text: Third, the Bill allows for conciliatory measures, such as mediation, as well as voluntary cancellation or suspension of registration where there are concerns on the vet's fitness to practise.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: These measures, subject to the Council's approval, help to address issues through negotiation without defaulting to formal disciplinary proceedings.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Henry Kwek rightly said that the framework must guard against misuse, while preserving confidence and fairness.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The Council is, first and foremost, a regulator.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Its primary duty is to maintain professional standards, and not to promote or advocate the professions' interest.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: There are thus safeguards and clear lines of accountability back to the Government, which will ensure alignment with broader public interest.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The Veterinary Council President and members are appointed by the Minister, who can also remove members where necessary.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The Registrar is also appointed by the Minister and must be a public officer, or an officer or employee of a public authority.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: First, disciplinary proceedings must also include non-vets, such as legal professionals, to provide balanced and objective oversight.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Members with conflicts of interest must also recuse themselves from proceedings.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Second, the Bill prohibits certain individuals to review the same case along various stages of proceedings.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: For instance, the Registrar who reviewed and referred the case to the Council must not be appointed to a Complaints Assessment Committee, a Disciplinary Committee, or an Interim Orders Committee.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: A member of the Complaints Assessment Committee who conducted an inquiry in respect of a disciplinary case must not be appointed as a member or observer of a Disciplinary Committee on the same case.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Appeals do not return to the Council and the committees for reconsideration, ensuring that disciplinary decisions are subject to independent review, and safeguarding the interests of both vets and the public.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This appeal mechanism takes reference from the disciplinary framework of the human healthcare sector, including the dental and allied health professions.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Some Members have also mentioned about raising awareness, I think Mr Muhaimin mentioned that earlier.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: AVS will work with the Council to raise awareness and educate the public on its requirements and processes.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This includes information on the Council's webpage, which will contain information such as vets' class of registration and place of employment.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This can help the public identify vets with restricted registration, who may only practise in establishments recognised by the Council.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The Council will also publish a guide to support complainants seeking redress.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This will include steps on how to file a complaint, including how to make a statutory declaration.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This guide will also address Ms Lee Hui Ying and Mr Yip Hon Weng's queries on when a complainant should file a complaint with the Council or otherwise commence a civil proceeding.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: A complainant may pursue either or both, as the circumstances warrant.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This is consistent with how other professional regulatory frameworks in Singapore operate.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Ms Diana Pang asked about advertising standards for veterinary services and Mr Cai Yinzhou asked about minimum standards for non-conventional therapies.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The Code of Ethics for Veterinarians includes advertising standards for veterinary services, such as requiring information to be factual and not comparative.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Under the Code, a vet is also responsible for choosing the treatment regimens for his patients, based on sound, evidence-based science and practice and/or diagnostic test results.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This is applicable to non-conventional novel therapies as well.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Many Members also raised concerns about the affordability of care and transparency of costs.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I have heard that as well in my interactions with vets and also the broader public.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This Code also requires vets to clearly explain treatment options, risks and costs, to obtain consent from owners for the treatment of their animal, and avoid unnecessary procedures.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Vets should also provide pet owners with an estimate of fees.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: These standards ensure better pricing transparency and help to build trust between pet owners and vets by promoting professionalism and fairness.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Under this Bill, while vets will be subject to regulatory requirements, they will be similar to those under today's licensing regime under AVS.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Furthermore, provisions are in place to ensure a smooth transition for current practitioners into the new regime.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We are also looking at other measures to address this.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This includes listing fees to promote greater transparency.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We will update on the timeline when ready.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In addition, there are pet insurance schemes available in Singapore to help pet owners with the cost of vet services.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: There are also professional indemnity insurance schemes for vets to cover legal defence and settlement costs arising from allegations of professional negligence or misconduct.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We share Members' concerns on the need to be mindful of costs to animal owners and are closely monitoring the trends.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: To Mr Kenneth Tiong's questions on fees for registration and practising certificates, we will consider various factors including current cost trends and the impact on existing practices in determining the prescribed fees.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Owners are responsible for providing for their pets' needs, including medical care.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, we strongly encourage prospective pet owners to thoroughly consider the full cost of raising a pet before committing to becoming a pet owner.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I seek the House's full support for this Bill.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Minister of State Alvin Tan, would you like to respond?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, I thank the Minister of State for this comprehensive response.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: And I checked the figures just now, I think it is still around the same.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Basically, NParks is operating on a very, very lean budget.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: I have a lot of respect for NParks staff, but they have to handle a lot of things.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: And now, with public expectations, and from what we hear from the Chamber, this new regulation is a step-up, I do hope that the Government can provide a bit more resources to AVS, to discharge what the public expects of this new regulation regime.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Minister of State Alvin Tan, would you like to respond?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I think my AVS colleagues will be very encouraged by his appeal.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We will resource our AVS and NParks colleagues as necessary for them to conduct their important mission.

speaker: Mr David Hoe
text: I am specifically heartened to hear that we will explore a possible veterinary local degree.

speaker: Mr David Hoe
text: Specifically, could we consider a Higher Nitec course that could then feed into the polytechnic diploma-related course?

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Minister of State Alvin Tan, would you like to respond?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: As I mentioned earlier, we are looking at manpower projections as well as resource requirements to study a local programme.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We already have programmes with some polytechnics as well.
